title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 96-99): Grothendieck is building an explicit, coordinate-level description of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2 equipped with a 'Legendre pinning' (épinglage de Legendre). This is a rigidification of the double cover x: E → P^1 branched at the images of the 2-torsion.

The objects involved:
- J is a 4-element set: the branch points / 2-torsion.
- V_J = Ker(k^J → k, sum) is 3-dimensional.
- F_t ⊂ V_J is a 2-dimensional subspace, cut out by one more linear form Σ c_i λ_i = 0. Here (c_i) is determined up to k^* and up to adding a diagonal element, which encodes the cross-ratio / Legendre parameter.
- \underline t is the tangent line at the origin, and \underline t^* its dual.
- \underline ω = \underline ω_J is a 2-element set with an involution ω ↦ ω' = -ω, a torsor-like datum of 'square roots'.
- ν̌ : \underline t^{⊗2} ≅ F_t^{⊗2}(\underline ω) is a twisted isomorphism.
- α : μ_4^* ≅ \underline ω identifies the two primitive 4th roots of unity with \underline ω.

On the previous page the structure K is encoded by maps Ǩ_i(δ) = ψ^{ω_i}(δ) ∧ ω_i, with ψ^ω(δ) ∈ F_t. The conditions so far are:
- (71) ψ^{ω'}(δ) = i_ω ψ^ω(δ), where i_ω = α^{-1}(ω).
- (72) ψ^ω(λδ) = λ^{-1} ψ^ω(δ), homogeneity.

On this page the remaining condition (67) is written contragrediently as Ǩ_i^{⊗2}(δ̌^{⊗2}) = ν̌(δ̌^{⊗2}) ∧ ω_i. In terms of ψ this becomes (73) ψ^ω(δ)^{⊗2} = ν̌(δ̌^{⊗2}) ∧ ω.

A marginal NB observes that, given (71) and (72), the two relations (73) for the two ω are equivalent, and that it suffices to impose (73) for a single δ.

Lemma: Legendre pinnings with given data (J, F_t ⊂ V_J(k), \underline t, ν̌) are identified with systems (α, (ψ^ω(δ))_{(ω,δ) ∈ \underline ω × \underline t^*}) with values in F_t, satisfying (71), (72), (73).

Grothendieck then begins to make this fully explicit in coordinates. Via the embedding F_t ⊂ V_J ⊂ k^J, the family becomes a three-index family of scalars (74): ψ_i^ω(δ) ∈ k, for i ∈ J, ω ∈ \underline ω, δ ∈ \underline t^*. The next page writes out the resulting linear conditions (75)-(78) (sum zero, the analogues of (71)/(72), and Σ c_i ψ_i = 0) and then (73).

Purpose: an explicit, coordinate presentation of the moduli of elliptic curves with Legendre-type (2-torsion plus μ_4 / quarter-period) rigidification. It is presumably meant to compute the moduli scheme or stack and its automorphism groups by hand.
errors:
No mathematical error found. Consistency checks:
- Under δ ↦ λδ we have δ̌ ↦ λ^{-1}δ̌, so the right side of (73) scales by λ^{-2}, matching (72) on the left side.
- Under ω ↦ ω' = -ω, (71) gives ψ^{ω'}⊗2 = i^2 ψ^ω⊗2 = -ψ^ω⊗2, while the right side becomes ν̌ ∧ (-ω).
- So the marginal NB (the two (73) are equivalent, and one δ suffices) is correct.

ideas.what: Reformulating a Legendre-type rigidification of an elliptic curve as a family ψ^ω(δ) ∈ F_t indexed by \underline ω × \underline t^*, subject to equivariance (71), homogeneity (72) and a quadratic normalisation (73)
ideas.modern_name: Explicit description of a level structure / rigidification (Legendre level-2 structure with extra μ_4 datum) as a moduli functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre form classical; moduli with level structures: Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur

ideas.what: Coordinatisation through F_t ⊂ V_J = Ker(k^J → k): a three-index scalar family ψ_i^ω(δ)
ideas.modern_name: Linear-algebra coordinates on the 4-point configuration of P^1 (cross-ratio via the c_i)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine bookkeeping: an explicit parametrisation of Legendre pinnings in coordinates. It is internally consistent but contains no new concept or result beyond standard level-structure moduli theory.

'en termes des plongement' is likely 'Moyennant le plongement F_t ⊂ V_J = Ker(k^J → k)' (the sum map labelled 'somme').
